ai.description: This frog reaches 45–60 mm. It is brown with a distinct white upper lip, yellow spots on the flanks, and prominent triangular skin projections above the eyes. It belongs to the family Megophryidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys flavipunctata* is best identified by the presence of distinct, bright yellow spots scattered across its dark dorsal skin, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Megophrys flavipunctata* inhabits primary evergreen and subtropical broadleaf forests in the Eastern Himalayas, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Megophrys flavipunctata* is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among leaf litter during the day to ambush passing insect prey under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys flavipunctata* breeds in streams during the monsoon season. Females lay small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs attached to the undersides of submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Megophrys flavipunctata* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically within the Indian states of Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, at elevations between 1,000–2,000m.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Megophrys flavipunctata* consists of a series of short, low-pitched, metallic "clucks" emitted from within dense, humid montane forests.
